3.2.2.2-r10.burton_quote: Xenophon, and of which all fair persons may worthily brag, that a strong man must labour for his living if he will have aught, a valiant man must fight and endanger himself for it, a wise man speak

3.2.2.2-r11.burton_quote: and a Queen, that when she was to be trodden on by wild horses for a punishment, the wild beasts stood in admiration of her person (Saxo Grammaticus lib. 8 Dan. Hist.), and would not hurt her

3.2.2.2-r16.burton_quote: Every man sought to get her love, some with gallant and costly apparel, some with an affected pace, some with music, others with rich gifts

3.2.2.2-r17.burton_quote: in comeliness of person, and all good qualities far exceeding others; whensoever fair Charmides came abroad, they seemed all to be in love with him

3.2.2.2-r18.burton_quote: holds it no such indignity for the Trojans and Greeks to contend ten years, to spend so much labour

citations.display: Quintus Curtius Rufus, *History of Alexander*, book 1

3.2.2.2-r2.burton_quote: Such is their intemperance and lust, that they are as much maimed by report, as if they saw them

3.2.2.2-r20.burton_quote: as a candle in the dark his beauty shined, all men’s eyes (as Xenophon describes the manner of it) were instantly fixed on him

3.2.2.2-r21.burton_quote: he was wounded at the first sight, his heart panted and he could not possibly turn his eyes from her

3.2.2.2-r22.burton_quote: I will not conceal it, she overcame me with her presence, and quite assaulted my continency, which I had kept unto mine old age; I resisted a long time my bodily eyes
3.2.2.2-r22.translation: I am ashamed to say it

3.2.2.2-r23.burton_quote: though she come accompanied with the Graces, and all Cupid’s train to attend up on her, girt with her own girdle, and smell of Cinnamon and Balm, yet if she be bald or bad haired, she cannot please her Vulcan

3.2.2.2-r25.translation: For the eyes are the chief seat of beauty.

3.2.2.2-r26.translation: Ocelli ('Little Eyes'), poem 17, which Lipsius also mentions for its elegance

3.2.2.2-r29.burton_quote: that love is witchcraft, it gets in at our eyes, pores, nostrils, engenders the same qualities, and affections in us, as were in the party whence it came. The manner of the fascination, as Ficinus comm. 10 cap. con. in Plat. declares it, is thus: mortal men are then especially bewitched, when as by often gazing one on the other, they direct sight to sight, join eye to eye, and so drink and suck in Love between them; for the beginning of this disease is the Eye. And therefore he that hath a clear Eye

3.2.2.2-r3.burton_quote: Leucippe, Sostratus’ fair daughter, was far in love with her, and out of fame and common rumour, so much incensed, that he would needs have her to be his wife

3.2.2.2-r30.burton_quote: the purer spirits are infected, the one Eye pierceth through the other with his rays, which he sends forth

citations.display: Pedro Morales, *De pulchritudine Jesu et Mariae*
citations.raw: Lib. de pulch. Jes. et Mar.

3.2.2.2-r32.burton_quote: that by sight alone, make others blear-eyed: and it is more than manifest, that the vapour of the corrupt blood doth get in together with the rays, and so by the contagion, the spectator’s eyes are infected

3.2.2.2-r33.burton_quote: Fairies he spied in the wilderness

3.2.2.2-r34.burton_quote: Neither is it any wonder, if we but consider how many other diseases closely, and as suddenly are caught by infection, Plague, Itch, Scabs, Flux, &c.

3.2.2.2-r4.burton_quote: feign a kind of beauty to themselves

3.2.2.2-r5.burton_quote: than which in all Nature’s treasure (saith Isocrates) there is nothing so majestical and sacred, nothing so divine, lovely, precious, ’tis nature’s Crown, gold and glory; bonum si non summum, de summis tamen non infrequenter triumphans, whose power hence may be discerned

3.2.2.2-r7.burton_quote: wise, just, honest men, except with mutual offices and kindnesses, some good turn or other, they extort this love from us; only fair persons we love at first sight, desire their acquaintance, and adore them as so many Gods: we had rather serve them than command others, and account ourselves the more beholding to them

3.2.2.2-r9.burton_quote: for she was a most beautiful woman
